summary: E3 reports reference DNA read fraction .9466 and four listed non-reference read fractions .0265, .0125, .0075, and .0035, with listed variant lengths 378, 205, 498, and 608 nt. The listed fractions total .9966; the unlisted .0034 is unaccounted, not assumed absent. The evidence object has no explicit A/B condition label, sampling provenance, coverage, or sequencing pipeline. These are DNA read fractions only: they do not establish template fractions without assay calibration, transcript fractions, transcription efficiencies, or RNA concentrations. R4_S2 (2025-02-01 abstract) reports sequence-composition changes across amplification rounds in phage-display libraries, where biological propagation/selection differs from amplification of this in-vitro DNA template; it is weak analogy, not direct support. Other R4 hits are unrelated reviews or assays. T4 is delivered with G2 still open; issue E4 for labelled endpoint template-fraction measurements and R5 for direct defined-template amplification evidence.

hypotheses: H1 (new, unconfirmed): production-driven accumulation of connected RNA loop junctions outruns relaxation and traps internal solvent-rich domains after an effective-load threshold.
H1a (unverified bridge): terminal RNA loops provide reversible sticker contacts with sufficient connectivity and slow exchange for path-dependent arrest; R3_S3 gives architectural plausibility only.
H2 alternative: sequence/ionic composition determines equilibrium phase coexistence; schedule history disappears after matched final composition and equilibration.
H3 alternative: amplification changes DNA population or carries reaction components, affecting transcription or imaging.
